utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well here we are again. Mr. Stanisic is absent and his absence is very well explained in the two reports which we have received and I imagine the parties have also received. Have you received the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we received the report, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I will deal first with the report of the medical officer, Dr. Paulus Falke. It is dated the 13th of May. He says that for the past five days, including this morning, he examined Mr. Stanisic. Mr. Stanisic was losing blood with his bowel movements about six to eight times each day and that indeed, he says, was observed by the guards. He had a slight fever, unsteady on his legs and very tired. He could hardly participate in any social activity. His son was visiting him but twice, Mr. Stanisic had to terminate the visit after a short time owing to fatigue, following which he went back to his cell. As a result of all of that, Dr. Falke says he's planning to have him admitted into the penitentiary hospital this week so that his condition may be monitored and observed more closely and his initial proposal to the hospital staff will be for one week of close observation. Yesterday, Dr. Falke says he called Dr. Kazimir, the treating gastroenterologist, and discussed with him Mr. Stanisic's situation at length on the phone. He, that is, Dr. Kazimir, apologised to Dr. Falke about the delay of his reports. Dr. Falke says that he has an appointment with him later today to discuss the technical aspect of the reporting process in this case. They also discussed the medical treatment and made some changes. They both agreed that his bowel problem, the pouchitis, seems to invalidate him a great deal. Dr. Falke also discussed the condition of the accused with Dr. Petrovic, his treating psychiatrist. She agrees that there is a significant improvement in his depression but nonetheless advises strongly against the video conference link at this stage due to the fear of relapse. His condition is still vulnerable. He concludes by saying that although during the hearings of the 28th April, he mentioned that Mr. Stanisic could try to use the video conference link at some time in the future, he's of the same opinion as Dr. Petrovic at this time. You will remember that Dr. Petrovic had advised strongly against Mr. Stanisic using the video conference link. So that report is fairly detailed. We will learn later whether Mr. Stanisic has been admitted to hospital. We also have a report which again indicates that the procedures established by the Chamber last week are being complied with in terms of reporting. This comes from Mr. Fraser Gilmour and there's no need for me to go through that. It seems clear that we are not in a position to continue today in the absence of Mr. Stanisic. On the basis of this report, he's neither able to come to court nor to follow and participate in the proceedings by video conference link. Now, Mr. Groome, do you have any observations?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The only information that I would provide the Court, Your Honour, is that the witness that we had scheduled for this coming next Monday actually because of special travel arrangements that had to be made for that witness, it's a non-refundable ticket so if I might suggest, if it seems that he's going to be hospitalised this week, then maybe we would hopefully be able to try again Monday. As I say, the ticket is a non-refundable ticket so the witness will have to travel here or the Tribunal will lose the value of the ticket so perhaps that might be one way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, good morning. We, as Defence believe that based on the order of Your Honours of the 8th of May, there is ample reason to not continue today and based on the letter of Dr. Falke of the 13th of May, we submit to the Court that it might be considered to adjourn for this week in terms of the hospitalisation and as far as we know, Mr. Stanisic was brought to the hospital this morning although we don't have confirmation of that yet, but we were informed that indeed he is or will be brought today to the hospital. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I ask the views of the parties on this question. For how much longer can a responsible Chamber continue to come to court and not proceed with the trial in the circumstances where there is another accused awaiting trial? There is a measure that the Chamber can take. It would be a last resort, but we need to ensure, of course, that we are acting properly and that we have exhausted all other alternatives. As I indicated at the last session, this is a matter in which both parties have an interest and I'd like to just hear some views, even if they are preliminary, from the parties on that question. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, these views would be preliminary. I would ask for an opportunity to discuss this matter with the Prosecutor to give any final position. Bit it would seem to me, Your Honour, that what we know from the fitness hearing is that at least with respect to the pouchitis, we were told that there would be isolated temporary flare-ups from time to time and that they really shouldn't hold us back too much but they were something to be expected. And it seems that what we're facing today is exactly that, it's an isolated flare-up that I think we can expect hopefully this week to clear up and that should not reoccur for some period of time. With respect to the depression, all indications that are he's actually improving and here we have today that there's significant improvement so I think as frustrating as this is for all of us and as frustrating as it is for witnesses, I think it's important that we don't let that frustration affect our best decision in this matter. I agree with you severance would be the last possible -- or the last and most severe remedy to this problem but I don't believe we're anywhere near that at this stage. It's my expectation that next Monday or shortly thereafter, he will be physically able to use that videolink and it seems clear that his depression is lifting and that he will be able to participate. I do recognise, as does the Court, that there may come a time that we do have to have a difficult discussion and the Prosecution will have to adopt a position with respect to how we proceed. But I don't believe we're near that yet despite the enormous frustration, I think, that all of us are feeling at the stalled progress of the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have been at this for about two months. Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, our position as Defence counsel for Mr. Stanisic is still the same, that we still support the idea as ventilated earlier during the sessions that in order to have the defendant capable of attending trial or the video conference, it's not a matter of weeks but probably longer. May I recall that the letter of Dr. Falke of the 9th of May refers to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What do you mean by -- how much longer? You have made a submission on this, you said, previously? Just remind us what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Well, we rely on this in this regard on the prognosis of Dr. de Man who testified that it would take three until six months for a recovery in its full scope. This is what I refer to, Your Honour. We also as Defence counsel for Mr. Stanisic underline the need for an expeditious trial, yet we cannot ignore the situation as it is now. Even if the depression would be lifted at a certain moment, we're still dealing with the situation that the pouchitis and the annexed physical problems cannot be cured but only stabilised. Dr. Falke in his letter of the 9th of May refers to, "If the depression is lifted then I would opine that he may be capable of instructing counsel in the coming weeks." So of course we share the hope of Mr. Groome that by next week, the hospitalisation will have affected the accused in a positive way. We're still, of course, faced with the expectation of Dr. Falke as laid down in his letter of the 9th of May. I do recognise, of course, that a matter of severance of the cases is indeed procedurally an issue of last resort. Therefore I'm as Defence counsel of Mr. Stanisic quite hesitant to submit at this stage to the Court that such a request should be considered by the Court either proprio motu or should be initiated by the Prosecution or Defence counsel of Mr. Simatovic. It might be an idea to wait until next week what results came out of the hospitalisation but even if we take that into account that the physical state of the accused is -- will be such that he could technically attend videolink conference, we're still faced with the prognosis of both Dr. de Man and Dr. Falke as mentioned in his letter of the 9th of May that the question of the effective participation during the videolink conference is of grave concern, and I refer in this regard to paragraphs 12 and 13 of the order of the 8th of May where Your Honours also share the opinion that attending a videolink conference is one thing but participating in an effective way is another thing. So in sum, although we acknowledge the right for an expeditious trial and we as the Defence counsel of Mr. Stanisic have interest in such a trial in an expeditious way as well, we cannot ignore the situation that the full recovery of Mr. Stanisic might take longer than the week hospitalisation we are now facing. That being said, I don't think it's my position, I'm not in a position to initiate any severance proceedings or support that in this stage because I believe it's a matter of the Prosecution or Defence counsel of Mr. Simatovic, and that being said, I can understand the position of the Prosecutor that severance is a matter of last resort and therefore, we should maybe await the situation of this week and evaluate next week. I do agree that if next week, the situation of Mr. Stanisic would not be improved, either physically or mentally, that situation could form a basis for a new discussion. These are my submissions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. At the moment when we were discussing the possibility of continuing these proceedings and we have already preliminarily touched upon one of these arguments, the severance of these cases, the Defence has already said that it is against this, against the severance because we believe that it is necessary to, beforehand, make some decisions so that we can discuss this issue. For the time being, there is a decision by this Trial Chamber on the ability of the accused Stanisic to participate or to attend trial. The Trial Chamber has today said that we cannot continue work and it seems that this situation will continue throughout the rest of the week. The Prosecution has presented one of the problems that this poses which is bringing in witnesses and in this particular case, the impossibility of returning the tickets and thus incurring additional cost to this Tribunal. For these reasons and taking into account the fact that the Defence of the accused Simatovic also has to travel, we propose that if the Trial Chamber takes the position that this trial has to be adjourned for at least a period of time that Dr. Falke proposed in his report, we would be of the view that the Trial Chamber should not schedule the next trial or the next sitting until it is certain that Mr. Stanisic can attend. And I think we should first have a report from the doctor and then schedule a trial to avoid this situation of always being in the courtroom and then facing the situation that we cannot work on that day. I think this would also be useful to the Prosecution because then it would be able to bring the next witness on short notice and of course this would also be convenient to the Simatovic Defence in order for him to attend the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Jovanovic has a slightly different view of things. He's suggesting that we adjourn and only resume until such time as we are notified by the doctor that Mr. Stanisic is in a position to attend either court or the video conference link. What he did not say, of course, is that in the event that in such a situation, Mr. Stanisic chose not to attend either the court or the video conference link, then the Trial Chamber would have to consider seeing that conduct as a voluntary waiver of the right to be tried in one's presence. Both Mr. Knoops and Mr. Groome suggested adjourning until Monday of next week. This would be consistent with the report of Dr. Falke who said that his initial proposal to the hospital staff is that Mr. Stanisic remain for one week of close observation. Before I consult, I saw Mr. Groome rising.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There's just one other matter or one other suggestion I wanted to make to the Court. When the Court originally asked for suggestions or for positions on how we might proceed several months ago, one of the options the Court asked us to address was whether the Court should return the case to the pre-trial stage and so the Court could get on with other work of the Tribunal to conclude its business, to do other trials. I would note to the Chamber that there is another case that I am senior trial attorney on that had had a Pre-Trial Conference scheduled for this Friday. Maybe one of the things the Chamber could consider is whether that case could commence in the near future in a way that would allow the Court to schedule the two cases so that if some of the medical problems that Mr. Stanisic interfere with the ability of the Court to conduct hearings in this case, the Court might have the option of conducting hearings in that other case. I wouldn't want to say too much more without the presence of the attorneys on that case, it is Prosecutor v. Milan and Sredoje Lukic, but it may be something that the Court might want to consider as one way to operate more efficiently given the unusual circumstances which the Chamber faces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber is grateful to the parties for the submissions that they have made. We have found them helpful. We will adjourn until Monday of next week. We are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 19th of May, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 9.26 a.m.,
